2. A noisy writer with the actual bath retained

The encoded boundary

Let  $V_N$  be the fixed stabilizer encoder,  $C_s$  the accepted deterministic correction for valid syndrome  $s$ , and  $\pi_\beta$  the thermal syndrome distribution. The ideal target channel is

 $\mathcal E_{\beta,N}(\rho_{LR})
=
\sum_s \pi_\beta(s)
(C_sV_N\otimes I_R)\rho_{LR}
(V_N^\dagger C_s^\dagger\otimes I_R).$ The physical writer receives the unknown state through an ordinary fault-tolerant encoded boundary. Its input code and  $V_N$  depend on width and protection scale, independently of future gate choices. Every estimate retains the untouched reference  $R$ .

Known-state initialization uses the same construction with a known logical input and noisy physical resets. The boundary does not promise arbitrarily accurate loading of an unprotected unknown qubit through a noisy first operation.

An auxiliary sector where the stipulated bath is exactly usable

Take

 $H_{\mathrm{total}}=H_{\mathrm{memory}}\otimes I_{\mathrm{aux}},$ with a fixed density of ancillary qubits having zero Hamiltonian. On those ancillary qubits, every one-site Pauli has only zero Bohr frequency, so the same stipulated Davies generator becomes

 $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{aux}}(\rho)
=
\sum_{i,P\in\{X,Y,Z\}}
\gamma_{i,P}(0)(P_i\rho P_i-\rho).$ Thus the auxiliary bath has a state-independent Poisson-Pauli realization, including during active controls. The memory bath retains its nonunitary, syndrome-conditioned components.

For a primitive cell of duration  $\tau$  involving at most  $a$  auxiliary qubits,

 $r_{\mathrm b}\le 1-e^{-3a\gamma_{\max}\tau}.$ After grouping shared physical supports correctly, a conservative combination with the additional  $p$ -bounded primitive faults is

 $q_{\mathrm{eff}}\le \sqrt p+\sqrt{r_{\mathrm b}}.$ This bound does not require independence between primitive faults and past bath records. The accepted finite ordinary-FT rectangles then apply to the auxiliary factory in a sufficiently small, size-independent open operating regime.

This is a derived use of the specified bath. No circuit-noise oracle has replaced it.
